about: The boatswain's calls (plan N4.6), synthesised by tools/sound/pipe.mjs into the raw folder and listed in sounds.json with `from`. The call has two notes, low (the hand open) and high (the hand closed over the buoy), glides between them, and three tones: plain, warble (the fingers fluttering, the pitch undulating) and trill (the tongue rolled, the sound broken fast). The calls of about 1800 were not written down; these follow the calls as the Royal Navy kept them (the Still: one high plain note, ended sharply; Carry On after it; Haul: the low note is the pause, the high note the pull; Hoist rises, Veer and Lower fall) and are shortened to a game's pace. Each segment: `note` [from, to] with 0 the low note and 1 the high, `tone`, `s` seconds; or `rest` seconds.

calls.what: A course for the master (steer, come up, bear away, full and by): the short call that the word is passed, two quick high notes and a drop.
Tack (all hands about ship): the general call, the low note rising to a warbled high and falling, then Haul Taut, a short low note snapped up to the high.
Wear (all hands wear ship): the general call, then Veer, the high note gliding slowly down to the low.
Heave to: the general call cut short, then Belay, a held high note, a low catch and a high note cut off: make fast, she stops.
Make sail (battle, plain, all sail): Away Aloft, a trilled low note, then Hoist, the low note rising slowly to a high one held and warbled.
Shorten sail: Away Aloft, a trilled low note, then Lower, a high note gliding slowly down to a trilled low one.
Back a topsail (man the braces): Haul, three pulls, each a low note (the pause) snapped up to the high (the pull).
Fill (let draw): Heave Round, the notes rolling warbled from low to high and back, ending on the low.
Haul away, piped as she comes through the wind or round before it (tacked, wore), when the yards are swung: two quick pulls.
The Still: one high plain note, ended sharply; every man stops what he is doing. Piped when she misses stays. Shortened from the Navy's eight seconds.
Carry On: a short high note falling to the low; the work is done, the men go back to what they were doing.
Hands to the pumps (N6.8): the general call cut short, then three slow strokes of the pump brakes, each the low note rising to the high and falling back.
Fire party (N6.8): urgent, three trilled high notes, each cut short, with a quick drop after the last.
Clear the wreckage (N6.8): Away, a trilled low note, then two sharp chops, a high note snapped down to the low twice.
Relieve the watch (the general call that calls the hands): the low note rising to a warbled high held, then falling; it turns out the watch below and sends the other down at a change of watch.
